engagement_background.objective: Generate $0.54-$1.2 million in annual cost savings by strategically sourcing high-spend categories, while maintaining service/quality levels, aggregating Choice Health’s enterprise-wide purchasing power, and completing the effort by July 2024 to support value-creation goals.
engagement_background.scope_summary: Initial scope covers 12 spend categories (Fleet, Employee Benefits, Medical Supplies, Pharmacy, Medical Equipment, Temp Labor – Therapists & Nurses, Telecom, Commercial Print, Copiers/MFPs, Office Supplies, IT Hardware) representing approximately $17.7 million in annual spend and targeted savings of 3-15 % per category. Scope may be refined as data is collected; some categories (e.g., Pharmacy, Medical Equipment) have since been put on hold or de-scoped.
constraints_challenges: Supplier non-responsiveness to data requests, delaying baseline development
Risk of uncoordinated 'side conversations' with suppliers that could undermine unified negotiation strategy
Need for timely participation and feedback from Choice Health stakeholders despite limited bandwidth
Potential pushback from incumbents and internal stakeholders when switching suppliers or altering contracts
Aggressive six-month timeline to capture savings and meet PE value-creation schedule

procurement_environment.data_availability: Accounts-payable spend data (~$39 M) extracted from the ERP and provided to Treya; limited internal line-item usage data or centralized contract repository, requiring direct supplier outreach for detailed data.
procurement_environment.data_quality_notes: Multiple vendor naming conventions, unmapped GL descriptions, and incomplete historical usage data—only a subset of high-spend suppliers have provided detailed files; remaining data cleanup and mapping needed before analysis.
